facts.assertion: GLA defines a Site Allocation as a site allocated for a particular type of development or use within a development plan.
GLA states allocated sites provide guidelines for planning decisions and promote development at borough level.
GLA states the published Site Allocation GIS boundaries are indicative and users should contact the relevant borough to confirm accuracy.
The GLA Site Allocations dataset is licensed under Open Government Licence v3.0.
The GLA Site Allocations page exposes a 5.11 MB GeoPackage in EPSG:27700 British National Grid.
The GLA Site Allocations page identifies GLA Planning as maintainer and Custom Polygons as the smallest geography.
The current GLA Planning Data Map FeatureServer exposes Site Allocations as layer 102 under Good Growth.
The current GLA Planning Data Map FeatureServer reports MaxRecordCount 21000 and JSON query support.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 is an esriGeometryPolygon feature layer.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 supports JSON, GeoJSON and PBF query formats.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 uses EPSG:27700 and reports an extent from easting 510675.096 to 554390.905 and northing 164588.646 to 200067.9904.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 reports support for advanced queries, statistics and standardized queries.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 reports pagination support.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 reports support for returning query extent and query with distance.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 schema includes sitename, address, borough, planningauthority, status, designation and classification fields.
GLA Site Allocations layer 102 schema includes source, hectares, easting and northing fields.
GLA Opportunity Areas layer 103 describes Opportunity Areas as major sources of brownfield land with significant development capacity.
GLA states Opportunity Area GIS boundaries are indicative and borough confirmation is required for accuracy.
GLA describes SHLAA layer 108 as a technical exercise for quantity and suitability of land potentially available for housing.
GLA explicitly states SHLAA is not a site allocations exercise; its web map identifies only sites already approved or formally allocated for housing.
